 817    ) -> Union[int, None]:
 818        """Insert a new party under the given type.
 819
 820        Parties are the leaf level of the hierarchy and represent
 821        transaction counterparties (e.g. "Tesco", "Netflix").
 822
 823        Args:
 824            name: Party name as extracted/cleaned from statements.
 825            type_id: FK to the parent `types` row.
 826            description: Optional human-readable description.
 827
 828        Returns:
 829            The `id` of the newly created party.
 830
 831        Raises:
 832            DatabaseError: If the (name, type_id) pair already exists,
 833                the parent type doesn't exist, or on any other database
 834                failure.
 835        """
 836        logger.debug(f"Adding party: {name} under type {type_id}")
 837
 838        try:
 839            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
 840                cursor = conn.cursor()
 841                cursor.execute(
 842                    "INSERT INTO parties (name, type_id, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
 843                    (name, type_id, description)
 844                )
 845                party_id = cursor.lastrowid
 846
 847            logger.info(f"Added party {party_id}: {name} under type {type_id}")
 848            return party_id
 849
 850        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
 851            error_msg = str(e).lower()
 852            if "unique" in error_msg:
 853                logger.warning(f"Duplicate party in type {type_id}: {name}")
 854                raise DatabaseError(f"Party already exists in this type: {name}") from e
 855            if "foreign key" in error_msg:
 856                logger.warning(f"Type {type_id} does not exist")
 857                raise DatabaseError(f"Type {type_id} does not exist") from e
 858            logger.error(f"Integrity error adding party: {e}")
 859            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e
 860        except Exception as e:
 861            logger.error(f"Failed to add party: {e}")
 862            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e

 864    def add_party_unknown_type(
 865        self,
 866        name: str,
 867        description: Optional[str] = None
 868    ) -> Union[int, None]:
 869        """Insert a new party under the auto-created "Unknown" hierarchy.
 870
 871        Ensures the full Unknown → Unknown → Unknown chain
 872        (category → sub_category → type) exists, creating it if needed,
 873        then inserts the party. Used during statement import when a
 874        transaction description can't be matched to a known party.
 875
 876        Args:
 877            name: Party name as extracted from the statement.
 878            description: Optional human-readable description.
 879
 880        Returns:
 881            The `id` of the newly created party.
 882
 883        Raises:
 884            DatabaseError: If the party already exists under the Unknown
 885                type, or on any other database failure.
 886        """
 887        logger.debug(f"Adding party with unknown type: {name}")
 888
 889        try:
 890            type_id = self._ensure_unknown_hierarchy()
 891            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
 892                cursor = conn.cursor()
 893                cursor.execute(
 894                    "INSERT INTO parties (name, type_id, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
 895                    (name, type_id, description)
 896                )
 897                party_id = cursor.lastrowid
 898
 899            logger.info(
 900                f"Added party {party_id}: {name} under unknown type {type_id}"
 901            )
 902            return party_id
 903
 904        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
 905            error_msg = str(e).lower()
 906            if "unique" in error_msg:
 907                logger.warning(f"Duplicate party in unknown type: {name}")
 908                raise DatabaseError(f"Party already exists in this type: {name}") from e
 909            if "foreign key" in error_msg:
 910                logger.error(f"Unknown type {type_id} unexpectedly missing")
 911                raise DatabaseError(f"Type {type_id} does not exist") from e
 912            logger.error(f"Integrity error adding party: {e}")
 913            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e
 914        except Exception as e:
 915            logger.error(f"Failed to add party: {e}")
 916            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e
 917
 918    def bulk_add_parties_unknown_type(self, names: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
 919        """Insert many parties under the Unknown type in one transaction.
 920
 921        Uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` so pre-existing parties are silently
 922        skipped, then reads back IDs for everything — new and
 923        pre-existing alike. Input names are deduplicated internally.
 924
 925        Designed for statement import, where dozens of new parties may
 926        appear at once.
 927
 928        Args:
 929            names: Party names to insert. Duplicates are ignored.
 930
 931        Returns:
 932            Mapping of `{name: party_id}` for every name in the input,
 933            whether newly inserted or already present.
 934
 935        Raises:
 936            DatabaseError: On any database failure.
 937        """
 938        if not names:
 939            return {}
 940
 941        type_id = self._ensure_unknown_hierarchy()
 942        # Defensive dedupe — callers shouldn't pass dupes, but don't blow up if they do
 943        unique_names = list(dict.fromkeys(names))
 944
 945        logger.info(f"Bulk inserting {len(unique_names)} parties under type {type_id}")
 946
 947        try:
 948            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
 949                cursor = conn.cursor()
 950
 951                # executemany keeps it to one round of Python→C marshalling
 952                cursor.executemany(
 953                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO parties (name, type_id, description) "
 954                    "VALUES (?, ?, NULL)",
 955                    [(n, type_id) for n in unique_names],
 956                )
 957                inserted = cursor.rowcount  # -1 on some drivers, but useful when it works
 958
 959                # Read back IDs for everything — new and pre-existing alike.
 960                # SQLite's param limit is 32,766 (since 3.32.0); 900 is fine.
 961                # Chunk if you ever expect >30k in one go.
 962                placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(unique_names))
 963                cursor.execute(
 964                    f"SELECT name, id FROM parties "
 965                    f"WHERE type_id = ? AND name IN ({placeholders})",
 966                    [type_id, *unique_names],
 967                )
 968                result = dict(cursor.fetchall())
 969
 970            logger.info(
 971                f"Bulk insert complete: {len(result)} ids returned "
 972                f"({inserted if inserted >= 0 else '?'} newly inserted)"
 973            )
 974            return result
 975
 976        except Exception as e:
 977            logger.error(f"Bulk party insert failed: {e}")
 978            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to bulk add parties: {e}") from e
 979
 980    def update_party(
 981        self,
 982        party_id: int,
 983        name: Optional[str] = None,
 984        type_id: Optional[int] = None,
 985        description: Optional[str] = None
 986    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 987        """Update a party's name and/or description.
 988
 989        Does not support changing `type_id` — use `remap_party()` for
 990        that, since it handles the `UNIQUE(name, type_id)` constraint
 991        by merging when a conflict exists and re-pointing transactions.
 992
 993        Args:
 994            party_id: Primary key of the party to update.
 995            name: New party name, if changing.
 996            type_id: Not allowed — raises `ValueError`. Use
 997                `remap_party()` instead.
 998            description: New description, if changing.
 999
1000        Returns:
1001            The updated party as a dict, or None if `party_id` does not
1002            exist.
1003
1004        Raises:
1005            ValueError: If `type_id` is provided.
1006            DatabaseError: If the new name conflicts with an existing
1007                party under the same type, or on any other database
1008                failure.
1009        """
1010        if type_id is not None:
1011            raise ValueError(
1012                "Cannot change type_id through update_party(). "
1013                "Use remap_party() instead, which handles potential "
1014                "merge conflicts with existing parties."
1015            )
1016
1017        try:
1018            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1019                cursor = conn.cursor()
1020
1021                updates = []
1022                params = []
1023                updated_fields = []
1024
1025                if name is not None:
1026                    updates.append("name = ?")
1027                    params.append(name)
1028                    updated_fields.append('name')
1029
1030                if description is not None:
1031                    updates.append("description = ?")
1032                    params.append(description)
1033                    updated_fields.append('description')
1034
1035                if not updates:
1036                    logger.debug(f"No fields to update for party {party_id}")
1037                    return self.get_party_by_id(party_id)
1038
1039                params.append(party_id)
1040                query = f"UPDATE parties SET {', '.join(updates)} WHERE id = ?"
1041                cursor.execute(query, params)
1042
1043                if cursor.rowcount == 0:
1044                    logger.debug(f"Party {party_id} not found for update")
1045                    return None
1046
1047            logger.info(f"Updated party {party_id}: {updated_fields}")
1048            return self.get_party_by_id(party_id)
1049
1050        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
1051            error_msg = str(e).lower()
1052            if "unique" in error_msg:
1053                logger.warning(f"Duplicate party name on update: {name}")
1054                raise DatabaseError(
1055                    f"A party named '{name}' already exists under this type"
1056                ) from e
1057            logger.error(f"Integrity error updating party {party_id}: {e}")
1058            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to update party: {e}") from e
1059        except Exception as e:
1060            logger.error(f"Failed to update party {party_id}: {e}")
1061            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to update party: {e}") from e
1062
1063    def remap_party(self, party_id: int, new_type_id: int) -> dict:
1064        """Move a party to a different type in the category hierarchy.
1065
1066        Handles the `UNIQUE(name, type_id)` constraint intelligently:
1067
1068        - If no party with the same name exists under the target type,
1069          simply updates `type_id` (a "remap").
1070        - If a same-named party already exists, merges: re-points all of
1071          the old party's transactions to the existing party, then
1072          deletes the old party row (a "merge").
1073
1074        This is the only method that should be used to change a party's
1075        `type_id`. See `update_party()` for name/description changes.
1076
1077        Args:
1078            party_id: Primary key of the party to move.
1079            new_type_id: Target type to move the party under.
1080
1081        Returns:
1082            Dict describing the outcome:
1083                - `{'action': 'none', ...}` — party already at target type.
1084                - `{'action': 'remapped', ...}` — `type_id` updated in place.
1085                - `{'action': 'merged', ...}` — transactions moved and old
1086                  party deleted. Includes `transactions_moved` count.
1087
1088        Raises:
1089            ValueError: If `party_id` or `new_type_id` does not exist.
1090            DatabaseError: On any other database failure.
1091        """
1092        try:
1093            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1094                cursor = conn.cursor()
1095
1096                # Get the party we're remapping
1097                cursor.execute(
1098                    "SELECT id, name, type_id FROM parties WHERE id = ?",
1099                    (party_id,)
1100                )
1101                party = cursor.fetchone()
1102
1103                if not party:
1104                    raise ValueError(f"Party {party_id} not found")
1105
1106                party_name = party['name']
1107                old_type_id = party['type_id']
1108
1109                # No-op check
1110                if old_type_id == new_type_id:
1111                    logger.info(
1112                        f"Party '{party_name}' (id={party_id}) already "
1113                        f"mapped to type_id={new_type_id}"
1114                    )
1115                    return {
1116                        'action': 'none',
1117                        'party_id': party_id,
1118                        'message': 'Party already mapped to this type',
1119                    }
1120
1121                # Validate target type exists
1122                cursor.execute(
1123                    "SELECT id FROM types WHERE id = ?",
1124                    (new_type_id,)
1125                )
1126                if not cursor.fetchone():
1127                    raise ValueError(f"Type {new_type_id} not found")
1128
1129                # Check for UNIQUE(name, type_id) conflict
1130                cursor.execute(
1131                    "SELECT id FROM parties "
1132                    "WHERE name = ? AND type_id = ? AND id != ?",
1133                    (party_name, new_type_id, party_id)
1134                )
1135                existing = cursor.fetchone()
1136
1137                if existing:
1138                    return self._merge_parties(
1139                        cursor, party_id, existing['id'],
1140                        party_name, new_type_id
1141                    )
1142                else:
1143                    return self._remap_party_type(
1144                        cursor, party_id, party_name,
1145                        old_type_id, new_type_id
1146                    )
1147
1148        except ValueError:
1149            raise
1150        except Exception as e:
1151            logger.error(f"Failed to remap party {party_id}: {e}")
1152            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to remap party: {e}") from e
1153
1154    def _merge_parties(
1155        self,
1156        cursor,
1157        old_party_id: int,
1158        target_party_id: int,
1159        party_name: str,
1160        new_type_id: int,
1161    ) -> dict:
1162        """Merge a party into an existing same-named party under the target type.
1163
1164        Re-points all transactions from `old_party_id` to
1165        `target_party_id`, then deletes the old party row. Called by
1166        `remap_party()` when a naming conflict is detected.
1167
1168        Args:
1169            cursor: Active database cursor (within a transaction).
1170            old_party_id: Party being merged away (will be deleted).
1171            target_party_id: Party that absorbs the transactions.
1172            party_name: Shared name (for logging).
1173            new_type_id: Target type ID (for logging).
1174
1175        Returns:
1176            Dict with `action='merged'`, both party IDs, and
1177            `transactions_moved` count.
1178        """
1179
1180        # Re-point transactions
1181        cursor.execute(
1182            "UPDATE transactions SET party_id = ? WHERE party_id = ?",
1183            (target_party_id, old_party_id)
1184        )
1185        transactions_moved = cursor.rowcount
1186
1187        # Re-point aliases if you have an aliases table
1188        # cursor.execute(
1189        #     "UPDATE party_aliases SET party_id = ? WHERE party_id = ?",
1190        #     (target_party_id, old_party_id)
1191        # )
1192
1193        # Delete the now-orphaned party
1194        cursor.execute(
1195            "DELETE FROM parties WHERE id = ?",
1196            (old_party_id,)
1197        )
1198
1199        logger.info(
1200            f"Merged party '{party_name}' (id={old_party_id}) into "
1201            f"existing party (id={target_party_id}) under "
1202            f"type_id={new_type_id}. "
1203            f"Moved {transactions_moved} transactions."
1204        )
1205
1206        return {
1207            'action': 'merged',
1208            'old_party_id': old_party_id,
1209            'new_party_id': target_party_id,
1210            'type_id': new_type_id,
1211            'transactions_moved': transactions_moved,
1212        }
1213
1214    def _remap_party_type(
1215        self,
1216        cursor,
1217        party_id: int,
1218        party_name: str,
1219        old_type_id: int,
1220        new_type_id: int,
1221    ) -> dict:
1222        """Update a party's `type_id` when no naming conflict exists.
1223
1224        Called by `remap_party()` for the simple case.
1225
1226        Args:
1227            cursor: Active database cursor (within a transaction).
1228            party_id: Party to update.
1229            party_name: Current party name (for logging).
1230            old_type_id: Previous type ID (for logging).
1231            new_type_id: New type ID to set.
1232
1233        Returns:
1234            Dict with `action='remapped'`, party ID, old/new type IDs,
1235            and `transactions_affected` count.
1236        """
1237
1238        cursor.execute(
1239            "UPDATE parties SET type_id = ? WHERE id = ?",
1240            (new_type_id, party_id)
1241        )
1242
1243        cursor.execute(
1244            "SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM transactions WHERE party_id = ?",
1245            (party_id,)
1246        )
1247        tx_count = cursor.fetchone()['count']
1248
1249        logger.info(
1250            f"Remapped party '{party_name}' (id={party_id}) "
1251            f"from type_id={old_type_id} to type_id={new_type_id}. "
1252            f"{tx_count} transactions affected."
1253        )
1254
1255        return {
1256            'action': 'remapped',
1257            'party_id': party_id,
1258            'old_type_id': old_type_id,
1259            'new_type_id': new_type_id,
1260            'transactions_affected': tx_count,
1261        }
1262
1263    def get_party_by_id(self, party_id: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1264        """Fetch a single party by primary key.
1265
1266        Args:
1267            party_id: The party's `id` column value.
1268
1269        Returns:
1270            The party row as a dict, or None if no match.
1271
1272        Raises:
1273            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1274        """
1275        try:
1276            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1277                cursor = conn.cursor()
1278                cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM parties WHERE id = ?", (party_id,))
1279                row = cursor.fetchone()
1280
1281                if not row:
1282                    logger.debug(f"Party {party_id} not found")
1283                    return None
1284                return dict(row)
1285
1286        except Exception as e:
1287            logger.error(f"Failed to get party {party_id}: {e}")
1288            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get party: {e}") from e

1290    def get_all_parties_with_transaction_counts(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
1291        """Fetch every party with full hierarchy context and transaction counts.
1292
1293        Joins through the full hierarchy (`types` → `sub_categories` →
1294        `categories`) and LEFT JOINs `transactions` to produce a
1295        `transaction_count` for each party. Ordered by party name.
1296
1297        Returns:
1298            List of party dicts, each including `type_name`,
1299            `sub_category_id`, `sub_category_name`, `category_id`,
1300            `category_name`, and `transaction_count`. Empty list if no
1301            parties exist.
1302
1303        Raises:
1304            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1305        """
1306        try:
1307            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1308                cursor = conn.cursor()
1309                cursor.execute('''
1310                    SELECT p.*, 
1311                        t.type as type_name,
1312                        sc.id as sub_category_id,
1313                        sc.sub_category as sub_category_name,
1314                        c.id as category_id,
1315                        c.category as category_name,
1316                        COUNT(tr.id) as transaction_count
1317                    FROM parties p
1318                    JOIN types t ON p.type_id = t.id
1319                    JOIN sub_categories sc ON t.sub_category_id = sc.id
1320                    JOIN categories c ON sc.category_id = c.id
1321                    LEFT JOIN transactions tr ON tr.party_id = p.id
1322                    GROUP BY p.id
1323                    ORDER BY p.name
1324                ''')
1325                rows = cursor.fetchall()
1326
1327                logger.debug(f"Retrieved {len(rows)} parties with transaction counts")
1328                return [dict(row) for row in rows]
1329
1330        except Exception as e:
1331            logger.error(f"Failed to get parties with counts: {e}")
1332            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get parties: {e}") from e
1333
1334    def get_parties_by_type(self, type_id: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:

1339
1340        Returns:

1342            type has no parties (or doesn't exist).

1344        Raises:
1345            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1346        """

1349                cursor = conn.cursor()
1350                cursor.execute(
1351                    "SELECT * FROM parties WHERE type_id = ? ORDER BY name",
1352                    (type_id,)
1353                )
1354                rows = cursor.fetchall()
1355
1356                logger.debug(f"Retrieved {len(rows)} parties for type {type_id}")
1357                return [dict(row) for row in rows]
1358
1359        except Exception as e:
1360            logger.error(f"Failed to get parties for type {type_id}: {e}")
1361            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get parties: {e}") from e

1363    def delete_party(self, party_id: int) -> bool:
1364        """Delete a party by primary key.
1365
1366        Refuses to delete if the party has any linked transactions,
1367        matching the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` constraint on
1368        `transactions.party_id`.
1369
1370        Args:
1371            party_id: Primary key of the party to delete.
1372
1373        Returns:
1374            True if deleted, False if the party did not exist.
1375
1376        Raises:
1377            DatabaseError: If the party has associated transactions,
1378                or on any other database failure.
1379        """
1380        try:
1381            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1382                cursor = conn.cursor()
1383
1384                cursor.execute(
1385                    "SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM transactions WHERE party_id = ?",
1386                    (party_id,)
1387                )
1388                count = cursor.fetchone()['count']
1389
1390                if count > 0:
1391                    logger.warning(
1392                        f"Cannot delete party {party_id}: "
1393                        f"has {count} associated transactions"
1394                    )
1395                    raise DatabaseError(
1396                        f"Cannot delete party {party_id}: "
1397                        f"has {count} associated transaction(s)"
1398                    )
1399
1400                cursor.execute("DELETE FROM parties WHERE id = ?", (party_id,))
1401
1402                if cursor.rowcount == 0:
1403                    logger.debug(f"Party {party_id} not found for deletion")
1404                    return False
1405
1406                logger.info(f"Deleted party {party_id}")
1407                return True
1408
1409        except DatabaseError:
1410            raise
1411        except Exception as e:
1412            logger.error(f"Failed to delete party {party_id}: {e}")
1413            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to delete party: {e}") from e
1414
1415    def get_transactions_by_party(self, party_id: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
1416        """Fetch all transactions for a given party, with account info.
1417
1418        Joins to `accounts` to include `account_name` on each row.
1419        Ordered by transaction date descending (most recent first).
1420
1421        Args:
1422            party_id: Party to filter transactions by.
1423
1424        Returns:
1425            List of transaction dicts, each including `account_name`.
1426            Empty list if the party has no transactions.
1427
1428        Raises:
1429            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1430        """
1431        try:
1432            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1433                cursor = conn.cursor()
1434                cursor.execute('''
1435                    SELECT t.*, a.account_name
1436                    FROM transactions t
1437                    LEFT JOIN accounts a ON t.account_id = a.id
1438                    WHERE t.party_id = ?
1439                    ORDER BY t.transaction_date DESC
1440                ''', (party_id,))
1441                rows = cursor.fetchall()
1442
1443                logger.debug(f"Retrieved {len(rows)} transactions for party {party_id}")
1444                return [dict(row) for row in rows]
1445
1446        except Exception as e:
1447            logger.error(f"Failed to get transactions for party {party_id}: {e}")
1448            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get transactions: {e}") from e
1449

1452    def get_party_hierarchy(self, party_id: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1453        """Fetch the full four-level hierarchy path for a party.
1454
1455        Returns a single flat dict with IDs and names for each level:
1456        party → type → sub_category → category.
1457
1458        Args:
1459            party_id: The party to look up.
1460
1461        Returns:
1462            Dict with `party_id`, `party_name`, `type_id`, `type_name`,
1463            `sub_category_id`, `sub_category_name`, `category_id`, and
1464            `category_name`. None if the party doesn't exist.
1465
1466        Raises:
1467            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1468        """
1469        try:
1470            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1471                cursor = conn.cursor()
1472                cursor.execute('''
1473                    SELECT 
1474                        p.id as party_id,
1475                        p.name as party_name,
1476                        t.id as type_id,
1477                        t.type as type_name,
1478                        sc.id as sub_category_id,
1479                        sc.sub_category as sub_category_name,
1480                        c.id as category_id,
1481                        c.category as category_name
1482                    FROM parties p
1483                    JOIN types t ON p.type_id = t.id
1484                    JOIN sub_categories sc ON t.sub_category_id = sc.id
1485                    JOIN categories c ON sc.category_id = c.id
1486                    WHERE p.id = ?
1487                ''', (party_id,))
1488
1489                row = cursor.fetchone()
1490                if not row:
1491                    logger.debug(f"No hierarchy found for party {party_id}")
1492                    return None
1493                return dict(row)
1494
1495        except Exception as e:
1496            logger.error(f"Failed to get hierarchy for party {party_id}: {e}")
1497            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get party hierarchy: {e}") from e

1499    def get_all_party_aliases(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
1500        """Build a mapping of known description strings to party IDs.
1501
1502        Combines two sources, both upper-cased for case-insensitive
1503        matching:
1504            1. `cleaned_description` values from `transactions` — what
1505               the categorizer saw before.
1506            2. `name` values from `parties` — canonical party names.
1507
1508        Transaction descriptions take priority (added first via
1509        `setdefault`). The result is used by the auto-categorizer to
1510        match incoming transactions to known parties.
1511
1512        Returns:
1513            Dict of `{UPPERCASE_ALIAS: party_id}`. Empty dict if no
1514            parties or transactions exist.
1515
1516        Raises:
1517            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1518        """
1519        try:
1520            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1521                cursor = conn.cursor()
1522
1523                cursor.execute('''
1524                    SELECT DISTINCT 
1525                        t.cleaned_description as alias,
1526                        t.party_id
1527                    FROM transactions t
1528                    ORDER BY t.cleaned_description
1529                ''')
1530                alias_data = cursor.fetchall()
1531
1532                cursor.execute('''
1533                    SELECT DISTINCT 
1534                        p.name as alias,
1535                        p.id as party_id
1536                    FROM parties p
1537                    ORDER BY p.name
1538                ''')
1539                party_data = cursor.fetchall()
1540
1541            alias_mapping = {}
1542            for row in alias_data:
1543                if row['alias']:
1544                    alias_mapping.setdefault(row['alias'].upper(), row['party_id'])
1545            for row in party_data:
1546                if row['alias']:
1547                    alias_mapping.setdefault(row['alias'].upper(), row['party_id'])
1548
1549            logger.debug(
1550                f"Built alias mapping: {len(alias_mapping)} aliases "
1551                f"({len(alias_data)} from transactions, "
1552                f"{len(party_data)} from parties)"
1553            )
1554            return alias_mapping
1555
1556        except Exception as e:
1557            logger.error(f"Failed to get party aliases: {e}")
1558            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get party aliases: {e}") from e
1559
1560    def _ensure_unknown_hierarchy(self) -> int:
1561        """Ensure the "Unknown" category/subcategory/type chain exists.
1562
1563        Creates any missing levels of the hierarchy:
1564            Unknown (category) → Unknown (sub_category) → Unknown (type)
1565
1566        The resulting type ID is cached on the instance so subsequent
1567        calls skip the database entirely.
1568
1569        Returns:
1570            The `id` of the "Unknown" type row.
1571        """
1572        if self._unknown_type_id is not None:
1573            logger.debug(
1574                f"Unknown hierarchy type_id resolved from cache: "
1575                f"{self._unknown_type_id}"
1576            )
1577            return self._unknown_type_id
1578
1579        logger.debug("Ensuring 'Unknown' hierarchy exists")
1580
1581        unknown_category = self.br.select_query(
1582            "SELECT id FROM categories WHERE category = ?",
1583            ("Unknown",)
1584        )
1585        if unknown_category:
1586            category_id = unknown_category['id']
1587        else:
1588            category_id = self.add_category("Unknown", "Automatically created unknown category")
1589            logger.info(f"Created 'Unknown' category: {category_id}")
1590
1591        unknown_sub_category = self.br.select_query(
1592            "SELECT id FROM sub_categories WHERE sub_category = ? AND category_id = ?",
1593            ("Unknown", category_id)
1594        )
1595        if unknown_sub_category:
1596            sub_category_id = unknown_sub_category['id']
1597        else:
1598            sub_category_id = self.add_sub_category(
1599                "Unknown", category_id, "Automatically created unknown sub-category"
1600            )
1601            logger.info(f"Created 'Unknown' sub-category: {sub_category_id}")
1602
1603        unknown_type = self.br.select_query(
1604            "SELECT id FROM types WHERE type = ? AND sub_category_id = ?",
1605            ("Unknown", sub_category_id)
1606        )
1607        if unknown_type:
1608            type_id = unknown_type['id']
1609        else:
1610            type_id = self.add_type(
1611                "Unknown", sub_category_id, "Automatically created unknown type"
1612            )
1613            logger.info(f"Created 'Unknown' type: {type_id}")
1614
1615        self._unknown_type_id = type_id
1616        logger.debug(f"Unknown hierarchy type_id cached: {type_id}")
1617        return self._unknown_type_id
1618
1619    def prime_unknown_type_cache(self) -> int:
1620        """Eagerly resolve and cache the "Unknown" type ID.
1621
1622        Call before batch operations that may create many new parties
1623        (e.g. statement import) so the hierarchy lookup and potential
1624        creation happens once, up front, rather than on the first
1625        `add_party_unknown_type()` call.
1626
1627        Returns:
1628            The cached "Unknown" type `id`.
1629        """
1630        return self._ensure_unknown_hierarchy()

Data-access layer for the category hierarchy tables.

Covers four tables — categories, sub_categories, types, and parties — plus cross-cutting concerns like party remapping, alias resolution, and the auto-created "Unknown" fallback hierarchy.

Methods are grouped by table, then by CRUD operation, with hierarchy and utility methods at the end.

Attributes:
  • db: The default ConnectionManager instance.
  • br: Shared BaseRepository helper for common query patterns.
  • _unknown_type_id: Cached ID of the "Unknown" type. Populated lazily by _ensure_unknown_hierarchy() on first use.

100        """Update one or more fields on an existing category.
101
102        Only non-None arguments are applied. Passing no updatable fields

118        try:

121
122                updates = []

124                updated_fields = []
125
126                if category is not None:

266        """Insert a new subcategory under the given category.
267
268        Args:

273        Returns:

694    def get_all_types(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
695        """Fetch every type with full hierarchy context.
696
697        Joins through `sub_categories` and `categories` to include
698        `sub_category_name`, `category_id`, and `category_name` in each
699        row. Ordered by category → subcategory → type name.
700
701        Returns:
702            List of type dicts with hierarchy fields. Empty list if no
703            types exist.
704
705        Raises:
706            DatabaseError: On query failure.
707        """
708        try:
709            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
710                cursor = conn.cursor()
711                cursor.execute('''
712                    SELECT t.*, sc.sub_category as sub_category_name, 
713                        c.id as category_id, c.category as category_name
714                    FROM types t
715                    JOIN sub_categories sc ON t.sub_category_id = sc.id
716                    JOIN categories c ON sc.category_id = c.id
717                    ORDER BY c.category, sc.sub_category, t.type
718                ''')
719                rows = cursor.fetchall()
720
721                logger.debug(f"Retrieved {len(rows)} types")
722                return [dict(row) for row in rows]
723

725            logger.error(f"Failed to get all types: {e}")
726            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get types: {e}") from e

759    def delete_type(self, type_id: int) -> bool:
760        """Delete a type by primary key.
761
762        Refuses to delete if the type has any child parties, matching
763        the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` constraint on `parties.type_id`.
764
765        Args:
766            type_id: Primary key of the type to delete.
767
768        Returns:
769            True if deleted, False if the type did not exist.
770
771        Raises:
772            DatabaseError: If the type has associated parties, or on
773                any other database failure.
774        """
775        try:
776            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
777                cursor = conn.cursor()
778
779                cursor.execute(
780                    "SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM parties WHERE type_id = ?",
781                    (type_id,)
782                )
783                count = cursor.fetchone()['count']
784
785                if count > 0:
786                    logger.warning(
787                        f"Cannot delete type {type_id}: "
788                        f"has {count} associated parties"
789                    )
790                    raise DatabaseError(
791                        f"Cannot delete type {type_id}: "
792                        f"has {count} associated party(ies)"
793                    )
794
795                cursor.execute("DELETE FROM types WHERE id = ?", (type_id,))
796
797                if cursor.rowcount == 0:
798                    logger.debug(f"Type {type_id} not found for deletion")
799                    return False
800
801                logger.info(f"Deleted type {type_id}")
802                return True
803
804        except DatabaseError:
805            raise
806        except Exception as e:
807            logger.error(f"Failed to delete type {type_id}: {e}")
808            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to delete type: {e}") from e

812    def add_party(
813        self,
814        name: str,
815        type_id: int,
816        description: Optional[str] = None
817    ) -> Union[int, None]:
818        """Insert a new party under the given type.
819
820        Parties are the leaf level of the hierarchy and represent
821        transaction counterparties (e.g. "Tesco", "Netflix").
822
823        Args:
824            name: Party name as extracted/cleaned from statements.
825            type_id: FK to the parent `types` row.
826            description: Optional human-readable description.
827
828        Returns:
829            The `id` of the newly created party.
830
831        Raises:
832            DatabaseError: If the (name, type_id) pair already exists,
833                the parent type doesn't exist, or on any other database
834                failure.
835        """
836        logger.debug(f"Adding party: {name} under type {type_id}")
837
838        try:
839            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
840                cursor = conn.cursor()
841                cursor.execute(
842                    "INSERT INTO parties (name, type_id, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
843                    (name, type_id, description)
844                )
845                party_id = cursor.lastrowid
846
847            logger.info(f"Added party {party_id}: {name} under type {type_id}")
848            return party_id
849
850        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
851            error_msg = str(e).lower()
852            if "unique" in error_msg:
853                logger.warning(f"Duplicate party in type {type_id}: {name}")
854                raise DatabaseError(f"Party already exists in this type: {name}") from e
855            if "foreign key" in error_msg:
856                logger.warning(f"Type {type_id} does not exist")
857                raise DatabaseError(f"Type {type_id} does not exist") from e
858            logger.error(f"Integrity error adding party: {e}")
859            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e
860        except Exception as e:
861            logger.error(f"Failed to add party: {e}")
862            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to add party: {e}") from e

def bulk_add_parties_unknown_type(self, names: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]: 
918    def bulk_add_parties_unknown_type(self, names: list[str]) -> dict[str, int]:
919        """Insert many parties under the Unknown type in one transaction.
920
921        Uses `INSERT OR IGNORE` so pre-existing parties are silently
922        skipped, then reads back IDs for everything — new and
923        pre-existing alike. Input names are deduplicated internally.
924
925        Designed for statement import, where dozens of new parties may
926        appear at once.
927
928        Args:
929            names: Party names to insert. Duplicates are ignored.
930
931        Returns:
932            Mapping of `{name: party_id}` for every name in the input,
933            whether newly inserted or already present.
934
935        Raises:
936            DatabaseError: On any database failure.
937        """
938        if not names:
939            return {}
940
941        type_id = self._ensure_unknown_hierarchy()
942        # Defensive dedupe — callers shouldn't pass dupes, but don't blow up if they do
943        unique_names = list(dict.fromkeys(names))
944
945        logger.info(f"Bulk inserting {len(unique_names)} parties under type {type_id}")
946
947        try:
948            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
949                cursor = conn.cursor()
950
951                # executemany keeps it to one round of Python→C marshalling
952                cursor.executemany(
953                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO parties (name, type_id, description) "
954                    "VALUES (?, ?, NULL)",
955                    [(n, type_id) for n in unique_names],
956                )
957                inserted = cursor.rowcount  # -1 on some drivers, but useful when it works
958
959                # Read back IDs for everything — new and pre-existing alike.
960                # SQLite's param limit is 32,766 (since 3.32.0); 900 is fine.
961                # Chunk if you ever expect >30k in one go.
962                placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(unique_names))
963                cursor.execute(
964                    f"SELECT name, id FROM parties "
965                    f"WHERE type_id = ? AND name IN ({placeholders})",
966                    [type_id, *unique_names],
967                )
968                result = dict(cursor.fetchall())
969
970            logger.info(
971                f"Bulk insert complete: {len(result)} ids returned "
972                f"({inserted if inserted >= 0 else '?'} newly inserted)"
973            )
974            return result
975
976        except Exception as e:
977            logger.error(f"Bulk party insert failed: {e}")
978            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to bulk add parties: {e}") from e

 980    def update_party(
 981        self,
 982        party_id: int,
 983        name: Optional[str] = None,
 984        type_id: Optional[int] = None,
 985        description: Optional[str] = None
 986    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 987        """Update a party's name and/or description.
 988
 989        Does not support changing `type_id` — use `remap_party()` for
 990        that, since it handles the `UNIQUE(name, type_id)` constraint
 991        by merging when a conflict exists and re-pointing transactions.
 992
 993        Args:
 994            party_id: Primary key of the party to update.
 995            name: New party name, if changing.
 996            type_id: Not allowed — raises `ValueError`. Use
 997                `remap_party()` instead.
 998            description: New description, if changing.
 999
1000        Returns:
1001            The updated party as a dict, or None if `party_id` does not
1002            exist.
1003
1004        Raises:
1005            ValueError: If `type_id` is provided.
1006            DatabaseError: If the new name conflicts with an existing
1007                party under the same type, or on any other database
1008                failure.
1009        """
1010        if type_id is not None:
1011            raise ValueError(
1012                "Cannot change type_id through update_party(). "
1013                "Use remap_party() instead, which handles potential "
1014                "merge conflicts with existing parties."
1015            )
1016
1017        try:
1018            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1019                cursor = conn.cursor()
1020
1021                updates = []
1022                params = []
1023                updated_fields = []
1024
1025                if name is not None:
1026                    updates.append("name = ?")
1027                    params.append(name)
1028                    updated_fields.append('name')
1029
1030                if description is not None:
1031                    updates.append("description = ?")
1032                    params.append(description)
1033                    updated_fields.append('description')
1034
1035                if not updates:
1036                    logger.debug(f"No fields to update for party {party_id}")
1037                    return self.get_party_by_id(party_id)
1038
1039                params.append(party_id)
1040                query = f"UPDATE parties SET {', '.join(updates)} WHERE id = ?"
1041                cursor.execute(query, params)
1042
1043                if cursor.rowcount == 0:
1044                    logger.debug(f"Party {party_id} not found for update")
1045                    return None
1046
1047            logger.info(f"Updated party {party_id}: {updated_fields}")
1048            return self.get_party_by_id(party_id)
1049
1050        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
1051            error_msg = str(e).lower()
1052            if "unique" in error_msg:
1053                logger.warning(f"Duplicate party name on update: {name}")
1054                raise DatabaseError(
1055                    f"A party named '{name}' already exists under this type"
1056                ) from e
1057            logger.error(f"Integrity error updating party {party_id}: {e}")
1058            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to update party: {e}") from e
1059        except Exception as e:
1060            logger.error(f"Failed to update party {party_id}: {e}")
1061            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to update party: {e}") from e

def remap_party(self, party_id: int, new_type_id: int) -> dict: 
1063    def remap_party(self, party_id: int, new_type_id: int) -> dict:
1064        """Move a party to a different type in the category hierarchy.
1065
1066        Handles the `UNIQUE(name, type_id)` constraint intelligently:
1067
1068        - If no party with the same name exists under the target type,
1069          simply updates `type_id` (a "remap").
1070        - If a same-named party already exists, merges: re-points all of
1071          the old party's transactions to the existing party, then
1072          deletes the old party row (a "merge").
1073
1074        This is the only method that should be used to change a party's
1075        `type_id`. See `update_party()` for name/description changes.
1076
1077        Args:
1078            party_id: Primary key of the party to move.
1079            new_type_id: Target type to move the party under.
1080
1081        Returns:
1082            Dict describing the outcome:
1083                - `{'action': 'none', ...}` — party already at target type.
1084                - `{'action': 'remapped', ...}` — `type_id` updated in place.
1085                - `{'action': 'merged', ...}` — transactions moved and old
1086                  party deleted. Includes `transactions_moved` count.
1087
1088        Raises:
1089            ValueError: If `party_id` or `new_type_id` does not exist.
1090            DatabaseError: On any other database failure.
1091        """
1092        try:
1093            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1094                cursor = conn.cursor()
1095
1096                # Get the party we're remapping
1097                cursor.execute(
1098                    "SELECT id, name, type_id FROM parties WHERE id = ?",
1099                    (party_id,)
1100                )
1101                party = cursor.fetchone()
1102
1103                if not party:
1104                    raise ValueError(f"Party {party_id} not found")
1105
1106                party_name = party['name']
1107                old_type_id = party['type_id']
1108
1109                # No-op check
1110                if old_type_id == new_type_id:
1111                    logger.info(
1112                        f"Party '{party_name}' (id={party_id}) already "
1113                        f"mapped to type_id={new_type_id}"
1114                    )
1115                    return {
1116                        'action': 'none',
1117                        'party_id': party_id,
1118                        'message': 'Party already mapped to this type',
1119                    }
1120
1121                # Validate target type exists
1122                cursor.execute(
1123                    "SELECT id FROM types WHERE id = ?",
1124                    (new_type_id,)
1125                )
1126                if not cursor.fetchone():
1127                    raise ValueError(f"Type {new_type_id} not found")
1128
1129                # Check for UNIQUE(name, type_id) conflict
1130                cursor.execute(
1131                    "SELECT id FROM parties "
1132                    "WHERE name = ? AND type_id = ? AND id != ?",
1133                    (party_name, new_type_id, party_id)
1134                )
1135                existing = cursor.fetchone()
1136
1137                if existing:
1138                    return self._merge_parties(
1139                        cursor, party_id, existing['id'],
1140                        party_name, new_type_id
1141                    )
1142                else:
1143                    return self._remap_party_type(
1144                        cursor, party_id, party_name,
1145                        old_type_id, new_type_id
1146                    )
1147
1148        except ValueError:
1149            raise
1150        except Exception as e:
1151            logger.error(f"Failed to remap party {party_id}: {e}")
1152            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to remap party: {e}") from e

  • If no party with the same name exists under the target type, simply updates type_id (a "remap").
  • If a same-named party already exists, merges: re-points all of the old party's transactions to the existing party, then deletes the old party row (a "merge").

This is the only method that should be used to change a party's type_id. See update_party() for name/description changes.

Arguments:

Returns:

Dict describing the outcome: - {'action': 'none', ...} — party already at target type. - {'action': 'remapped', ...} — type_id updated in place. - {'action': 'merged', ...} — transactions moved and old party deleted. Includes transactions_moved count.

Raises:

1297        Returns:

1299            `sub_category_id`, `sub_category_name`, `category_id`,
1300            `category_name`, and `transaction_count`. Empty list if no
1301            parties exist.
1302
1303        Raises:
1304            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1305        """
1306        try:
1307            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1308                cursor = conn.cursor()
1309                cursor.execute('''
1310                    SELECT p.*, 
1311                        t.type as type_name,
1312                        sc.id as sub_category_id,
1313                        sc.sub_category as sub_category_name,
1314                        c.id as category_id,
1315                        c.category as category_name,
1316                        COUNT(tr.id) as transaction_count
1317                    FROM parties p
1318                    JOIN types t ON p.type_id = t.id
1319                    JOIN sub_categories sc ON t.sub_category_id = sc.id
1320                    JOIN categories c ON sc.category_id = c.id
1321                    LEFT JOIN transactions tr ON tr.party_id = p.id
1322                    GROUP BY p.id
1323                    ORDER BY p.name
1324                ''')
1325                rows = cursor.fetchall()
1326
1327                logger.debug(f"Retrieved {len(rows)} parties with transaction counts")
1328                return [dict(row) for row in rows]
1329
1330        except Exception as e:
1331            logger.error(f"Failed to get parties with counts: {e}")
1332            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get parties: {e}") from e

def delete_party(self, party_id: int) -> bool: 
1363    def delete_party(self, party_id: int) -> bool:
1364        """Delete a party by primary key.
1365
1366        Refuses to delete if the party has any linked transactions,
1367        matching the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` constraint on
1368        `transactions.party_id`.
1369
1370        Args:
1371            party_id: Primary key of the party to delete.
1372
1373        Returns:
1374            True if deleted, False if the party did not exist.
1375
1376        Raises:
1377            DatabaseError: If the party has associated transactions,
1378                or on any other database failure.
1379        """
1380        try:
1381            with self.db.transaction() as conn:
1382                cursor = conn.cursor()
1383
1384                cursor.execute(
1385                    "SELECT COUNT(*) as count FROM transactions WHERE party_id = ?",
1386                    (party_id,)
1387                )
1388                count = cursor.fetchone()['count']
1389
1390                if count > 0:
1391                    logger.warning(
1392                        f"Cannot delete party {party_id}: "
1393                        f"has {count} associated transactions"
1394                    )
1395                    raise DatabaseError(
1396                        f"Cannot delete party {party_id}: "
1397                        f"has {count} associated transaction(s)"
1398                    )
1399
1400                cursor.execute("DELETE FROM parties WHERE id = ?", (party_id,))
1401
1402                if cursor.rowcount == 0:
1403                    logger.debug(f"Party {party_id} not found for deletion")
1404                    return False
1405
1406                logger.info(f"Deleted party {party_id}")
1407                return True
1408
1409        except DatabaseError:
1410            raise
1411        except Exception as e:
1412            logger.error(f"Failed to delete party {party_id}: {e}")
1413            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to delete party: {e}") from e

1452    def get_party_hierarchy(self, party_id: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
1453        """Fetch the full four-level hierarchy path for a party.
1454
1455        Returns a single flat dict with IDs and names for each level:
1456        party → type → sub_category → category.
1457
1458        Args:
1459            party_id: The party to look up.
1460
1461        Returns:
1462            Dict with `party_id`, `party_name`, `type_id`, `type_name`,
1463            `sub_category_id`, `sub_category_name`, `category_id`, and
1464            `category_name`. None if the party doesn't exist.
1465
1466        Raises:
1467            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1468        """
1469        try:
1470            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1471                cursor = conn.cursor()
1472                cursor.execute('''
1473                    SELECT 
1474                        p.id as party_id,
1475                        p.name as party_name,
1476                        t.id as type_id,
1477                        t.type as type_name,
1478                        sc.id as sub_category_id,
1479                        sc.sub_category as sub_category_name,
1480                        c.id as category_id,
1481                        c.category as category_name
1482                    FROM parties p
1483                    JOIN types t ON p.type_id = t.id
1484                    JOIN sub_categories sc ON t.sub_category_id = sc.id
1485                    JOIN categories c ON sc.category_id = c.id
1486                    WHERE p.id = ?
1487                ''', (party_id,))
1488
1489                row = cursor.fetchone()
1490                if not row:
1491                    logger.debug(f"No hierarchy found for party {party_id}")
1492                    return None
1493                return dict(row)
1494
1495        except Exception as e:
1496            logger.error(f"Failed to get hierarchy for party {party_id}: {e}")
1497            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get party hierarchy: {e}") from e

def get_all_party_aliases(self) -> Dict[str, int]: 
1499    def get_all_party_aliases(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
1500        """Build a mapping of known description strings to party IDs.
1501
1502        Combines two sources, both upper-cased for case-insensitive
1503        matching:
1504            1. `cleaned_description` values from `transactions` — what
1505               the categorizer saw before.
1506            2. `name` values from `parties` — canonical party names.
1507
1508        Transaction descriptions take priority (added first via
1509        `setdefault`). The result is used by the auto-categorizer to
1510        match incoming transactions to known parties.
1511
1512        Returns:
1513            Dict of `{UPPERCASE_ALIAS: party_id}`. Empty dict if no
1514            parties or transactions exist.
1515
1516        Raises:
1517            DatabaseError: On query failure.
1518        """
1519        try:
1520            with self.db.get_connection() as conn:
1521                cursor = conn.cursor()
1522
1523                cursor.execute('''
1524                    SELECT DISTINCT 
1525                        t.cleaned_description as alias,
1526                        t.party_id
1527                    FROM transactions t
1528                    ORDER BY t.cleaned_description
1529                ''')
1530                alias_data = cursor.fetchall()
1531
1532                cursor.execute('''
1533                    SELECT DISTINCT 
1534                        p.name as alias,
1535                        p.id as party_id
1536                    FROM parties p
1537                    ORDER BY p.name
1538                ''')
1539                party_data = cursor.fetchall()
1540
1541            alias_mapping = {}
1542            for row in alias_data:
1543                if row['alias']:
1544                    alias_mapping.setdefault(row['alias'].upper(), row['party_id'])
1545            for row in party_data:
1546                if row['alias']:
1547                    alias_mapping.setdefault(row['alias'].upper(), row['party_id'])
1548
1549            logger.debug(
1550                f"Built alias mapping: {len(alias_mapping)} aliases "
1551                f"({len(alias_data)} from transactions, "
1552                f"{len(party_data)} from parties)"
1553            )
1554            return alias_mapping
1555
1556        except Exception as e:
1557            logger.error(f"Failed to get party aliases: {e}")
1558            raise DatabaseError(f"Failed to get party aliases: {e}") from e

Build a mapping of known description strings to party IDs.

Combines two sources, both upper-cased for case-insensitive matching: 1. cleaned_description values from transactions — what the categorizer saw before. 2. name values from parties — canonical party names.

Transaction descriptions take priority (added first via setdefault). The result is used by the auto-categorizer to match incoming transactions to known parties.

Returns:

Dict of {UPPERCASE_ALIAS: party_id}. Empty dict if no parties or transactions exist.

Raises:
  • DatabaseError: On query failure.
